To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the outage probability of the system can be reduced with increasing the energy harvesting efficiency and the throughput of the system can also be improved with increasing the energy efficiency of the system.
a two-way cognitive relay network that is equipped an energy-harvester and realistic relay transceiver is more vulnerable to the hardware impairments than the traditional relay networks.

the network performance can be improved significantly by employing the power splitting receiver architecture, the time division broadcast relaying protocol, the dual-source energy transfer, and the high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of source nodes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of transceiver imperfections in a realistic cognitive relay network with energy harvesting capability.
a practical two-way relay cognitive radio network that is equipped an energy-harvester.
the effects of transceiver imperfections on the outage and throughput of a cognitive network that employs energy harvesting relay.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system performance is significantly degraded due to the impairing effects of realistic transceiver.

the system with dual-source energy transfer, the time switching-based receiver structure, and the multiple access broadcast protocol is the best candidate for the two-way cognitive relay network in terms of both outage and throughput.

a combination of the time switching-based receiver structure and the dual-source energy transfer policies would be the most suitable choice for the two-way cognitive networks that is equipped with a wireless energy harvesting relay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the network with the power splitting-based relay receiver structure can achieve higher throughput than the one that is equipped with the time switching receiver.
the proposed system can be used to design the network for a wide range of applications that are sensitive to the outage probability and the throughput of the system.

a network with a power-splitting receiver structure is a good choice for the system that requires higher data rate, while a system with a time-splitting receiver structure can be considered for a low data rate network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the network with a combination of multiple access broadcast protocol, the power splitting-based architecture and dual-source energy transfer policies achieves higher network throughput and the lowest outage probability in the presence of realistic relay hardware impairments.
a combination of dual source energy transfer policy and power splitting-based receiver structure is more suitable for the network to be equipped with realistic transceiver.
the system designer should consider the practical effects of hardware impairments of transceiver on the performance of the system to be able to achieve the optimal performance.
